proof: A Core on its build defaults activates a signed document over the surface protocol and reports the generation, the signing key, the document digest and the bindings, with no credential, endpoint URL or signing key in what a client sees. A tampered document, an expired one, one carrying success_rate and one leaving no reviewer are each refused by code without disturbing the active generation. A task runs under the registry; a new generation revokes the model it used and the next run stops explicitly with MODEL_REVOKED naming that generation, with nothing dispatched on another model.
audit: ABSENT before this task: the gateway's catalog was hardcoded, so a binding, a price or a revocation needed a new build; nothing was signed or versioned and there were no role bindings.
limitations: The production-endpoint half of EPR-E2E-002 has not run (no credentials here; DR-M3-002 defers it). The registry filters and refuses but does not choose (EPR-016) or compile (EPR-004). A revoked model stops the run explicitly because the direct path has no prevalidated alternative; fallback arrives with EPR-005. stats_version is a reference only; materialization is EPR-015. Ed25519 signing uses ed25519-dalek, a new dependency under the docs/36 framework.
